reason: The cited evidence supports grain refinement and room-temperature strength improvement by Y2O3 in a different alloy system (NiCoCr superalloy) and confirms DED processing of a Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEA, but neither study addresses the proposed Ti- and Ni-rich HEA composition, high-temperature mechanical properties, or the claimed mechanisms of creep resistance and ductility enhancement. The key premise that Y2O3 will improve high-temperature strength, creep, and ductility in this specific HEA is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles refine grain size in NiCoCr-based superalloys processed by laser metal deposition
Y2O3 nanoparticles enhance room-temperature tensile strength in a NiCoCr-based superalloy
Y2O3 nanoparticles can be introduced via powder surface decoration prior to additive manufacturing
Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEA can form a single-phase FCC solid solution via DED
Grain refinement and nanoparticle dispersion will stabilize microstructure and improve high-temperature mechanical properties in the proposed HEA
